chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Ahmar, from Abdullah ibn Hammad, from Sayf al-Tammar, who said:

We were with Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), a group from the Shi'ah, in al-Hijr. So he said: "Is there an eye upon us?" Then we turned to the right and the left, but we did not see anyone, so we said: "There is no eye upon us."

He said: "By the Lord of the Ka'bah, and by the Lord of the structure"—three times—"if I had been between Musa and al-Khidr, I would have informed them that I am more knowledgeable than both of them, and I would have informed them of what was not in their possession. For Musa and al-Khidr (عليهما السلام) were given the knowledge of what had been, and they were not given the knowledge of what will be and what is to occur until the Hour is established. And we have inherited it from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) as an inheritance."

key_terms.السَّاعَةُ: the Hour, meaning the final establishment of the Day of Judgment
key_terms.الْبَنِيَّةِ: the structure or sacred building, referring to the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْحِجْرِ: al-Hijr, the area beside the Ka'bah where this gathering took place
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Ka'bah, by whose Lord the Imam swears an oath
key_terms.عَيْنٌ: a watcher or spying eye observing the group
key_terms.عِلْمَ مَا كَانَ: knowledge of what has already occurred
key_terms.عِلْمَ مَا يَكُونُ: knowledge of what will come to pass
key_terms.وِرَاثَةً: as an inheritance, indicating transmitted divine knowledge from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله)

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the Imam's inherited knowledge compared to Musa and al-Khidr (عليهما السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith presents Imam Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) speaking about the divinely inherited knowledge of the Imams from the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله). It distinguishes between knowledge of past events and knowledge of what will occur until the Hour, affirming a special inherited 'ilm within the framework of Imamate.
